covers: The ports of the Sega 315-5313 VDP as byte offsets from its first address, as vdp_r and vdp_w decode them (offset times 2); the VDP's own registers are in sega315_5313-regs

entries.name: data port read
entries.description: Reads one word of VRAM, VSRAM or CRAM at the current address.
entries.behaviour: Code 0 reads VRAM, 4 VSRAM, 8 CRAM, then adds register 0x0F to the address; there is no read-ahead word. Write codes (1, 3) and undefined codes return a random word and keep the address; code 5 returns 0. Any data read cancels a pending first control word.

entries.name: data port write
entries.description: Writes one word to VRAM, CRAM or VSRAM, or feeds an armed fill.
entries.behaviour: Cancels a pending first control word. An armed fill runs; otherwise the word is stored by code (1 VRAM, 3 CRAM, 5 VSRAM) and the address steps by register 0x0F, while read and undefined codes ignore the write. A byte write is copied into both halves, VRAM words are byte-swapped at an odd address, and nothing is queued.

entries.name: status
entries.description: Returns the status word; reading it changes nothing.
entries.behaviour: Bit 7 VINT pending, 5 sprite collision (cleared each frame), 4 odd frame (interlace), 3 VBLANK (1 with display off), 2 HBLANK, 0 PAL. Bits 9 (FIFO empty), 13, 12 and 10 read 1; bits 8 (FIFO full), 6 (sprite overflow), 1 (DMA busy), 15, 14 and 11 read 0.

entries.name: control port
entries.description: Takes a 16-bit control word: a register write, or half of a two-word command.
entries.behaviour: Bits 15:14 equal to 10 set VDP register (bits 12:8) to the low byte. Any other word, with none pending, starts a command: code bits 1:0 and address bits 13:0 are its bits 15:14 and 13:0. The next word, whatever it holds, gives code bits 5:2 (bits 7:4) and address bits 15:14 (bits 1:0); code bit 5 starts a DMA.

entries.name: HV counter
entries.description: Returns the vertical counter in the high byte and the horizontal counter in the low byte.
entries.behaviour: Both are live, with no latch. V is the scanline (plus 1 past 460 of 480 line time) through a table for the 224 or 240 line mode and NTSC or PAL that jumps back after the active area (NTSC 224: 0xEA then 0xE5). H is the line time scaled to 0..480, minus 0x49 above 0xF7.

entries.name: HV counter write
entries.description: A write to the HV counter is refused.
entries.behaviour: The write is logged as an attempt to write the HV counters and has no other effect.

sources.cites: logerror("Attempt to Write to HV counters!!\n");

entries.name: PSG write
entries.description: Feeds the sound chip behind the VDP.
entries.behaviour: The low byte of the data goes to the sound chip, and only when the low byte lane is written; a write that touches only the high byte lane does nothing.

entries.name: PSG read
entries.description: A read of the sound chip port returns 0.
entries.behaviour: The read is logged as an attempt to read the PSG and returns 0.

entries.name: unmapped
entries.description: Offsets of the block that the handlers do not decode.
entries.behaviour: A read returns 0 and a write is reported as a write to an unmapped VDP port and ignored.
